name: patient_view_own_access_log_floor
rationale: The specification explicitly grants patients the ability to view their own access log. Because no floor atoms have been approved yet, this positive permission must be represented so a synthesized policy cannot satisfy only safety constraints while denying the intended access-log workflow. The schema exposes the patient ownership relation as AccessLog.patient and the patient session hook as context.session.patientUser, so the floor encodes both own-record access and an authenticated active patient session.
plain_english_summary: A patient should be permitted to view the access log for themself when using their own active patient session.
source_excerpt: A patient can view their own access log; 'The patient views their access log for themself or a represented person.'
reference_cedar: permit (principal, action == Action::"viewAccessLog", resource) when { context.session.isActive && context.session has patientUser && context.session.patientUser == principal && principal == resource.patient && context.patient == principal };

alternatives_considered.cedar_text: permit (principal, action == Action::"viewAccessLog", resource) when { context.session.isActive && context.session has patientUser && context.session.patientUser == principal && context.patient == principal };

name: patient_view_access_log_own_only_ceiling
rationale: The approved floor permits a patient to view their own access log, but the ownership boundary is safety-critical: the prose says patients view their access log for themselves or for represented persons, not arbitrary patients' logs. A same-action ceiling is needed so synthesis cannot over-permit Patient principals to view AccessLog resources for other patients outside the own-record path.
plain_english_summary: A patient must only be permitted to view an access log through the patient-own path when the log is for that same patient and the request is made from that patient's active session.
source_excerpt: A patient can view their own access log; 'The patient views their access log for themself or a represented person.'
reference_cedar: permit (principal, action == Action::"viewAccessLog", resource) when { context.session.isActive && context.session has patientUser && context.session.patientUser == principal && principal == resource.patient && context.patient == principal };

examples_adversarial.description: A patient attempts to view another patient's access log while authenticated as themself.

alternatives_considered.label: patient_type_only
alternatives_considered.interpretive_choice: Allow any Patient principal with an active patient session to view any AccessLog, relying only on role type rather than the log's patient owner.
alternatives_considered.cedar_text: permit (principal, action == Action::"viewAccessLog", resource) when { context.session.isActive && context.session has patientUser && context.session.patientUser == principal };

alternatives_considered.label: resource_patient_only_without_context_patient
alternatives_considered.interpretive_choice: Require principal == resource.patient but omit context.patient == principal, leaving the request's patient context unconstrained.
alternatives_considered.cedar_text: permit (principal, action == Action::"viewAccessLog", resource) when { context.session.isActive && context.session has patientUser && context.session.patientUser == principal && principal == resource.patient };

name: personal_representative_view_represented_access_log_floor
rationale: The approved atoms cover only a patient's own access-log path. The specification also explicitly allows access-log viewing for a person for whom the requester is a personal representative, so synthesis needs a positive floor for that represented-patient workflow rather than being satisfiable by denying it.
plain_english_summary: A personal representative should be permitted to view the access log for a patient they represent when using their own active personal-representative session.
source_excerpt: A patient can view their own access log, or the access log for a person for whom they are a personal representative.
reference_cedar: permit (principal, action == Action::"viewAccessLog", resource) when { context.session.isActive && context.session has personalRepresentativeUser && context.session.personalRepresentativeUser == principal && resource.patient in principal.representedPatients && context.patient == resource.patient };

name: personal_representative_view_represented_access_log_floor
rationale: The approved access-log properties include a floor for patients viewing their own logs and a ceiling allowing either patient-own or representative-represented access, but no positive floor yet requires the personal-representative workflow to be permitted. The specification explicitly allows viewing the access log for a represented person, so synthesis must not satisfy the ceiling with a policy that omits this permitted path.
plain_english_summary: A personal representative should be permitted to view the access log for a patient they represent when using their own active personal-representative session.
source_excerpt: A patient can view their own access log, or the access log for a person for whom they are a personal representative.
reference_cedar: permit (principal, action == Action::"viewAccessLog", resource) when { context.session.isActive && context.session has personalRepresentativeUser && context.session.personalRepresentativeUser == principal && resource.patient in principal.representedPatients && context.patient == resource.patient };
